chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib and Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who pushed another man onto a third man, so he killed him, he (peace be upon him) said: 'The wergild (blood money) is upon the one who fell upon the man and killed him, for the guardians of the killed one.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the pushed one can demand the wergild from the one who pushed him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And if the pushed one was hit by anything (injured), then it is upon the pusher as well.'
ai.seo_question: How is blood money distributed when one person pushes another into a killer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distribution of blood money (diyah) in a chain-reaction killing, establishing that the direct killer pays the victim's heirs while the instigator compensates the intermediate victim for any resulting injuries. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between direct causation and secondary liability, ensuring equitable compensation among all parties involved in the incident.
